# [TFQ-1340] DTM0 finite-rule machine with total integer tape and fuel-bounded evaluator

## 1. Abstract & Formal Statement

A DTM0 machine is a designated halt state with a finite, left-biased list of rows (state, scanned symbol, next state, written symbol, move) over the two-symbol alphabet blank and marked; a configuration is a state, an integer head and a total tape Int to symbol; execute runs at most the stated fuel and returns halted, stuck or fuelExhausted.

### Governing Obligation
The definition carries no input encoding, no unbounded-run semantics, no halting predicate and no comparison with Mathlib Turing.TM0; fuel exhaustion is a bounded-evaluator result and not non-halting.

### Witness Audit
These are plain Lean structures and total functions; no Mathlib import. Rows with state equal to the halt state are never fired because the halt test comes first. The tape is an arbitrary function Int to symbol, so configurations include tapes with infinitely many marks; Mathlib's TM0 tape has finite support. Duplicate rows are allowed and resolved by list order. The definitions are faithful to a deterministic two-symbol Turing-style machine with a stay move, but no theorem relates them to any computability notion.
